answer: Each AI grader is issued a unique ferrous‑signed credential stored in a tamper‑proof quartz ledger; the credential also contains a hashed vine‑derived nonce that only the issuing node can recompute. Periodically a random jury of ten nodes is selected to audit a sample of recent grading transactions, verifying the nonce and cross‑checking the ferrous signature against the ledger. An attacker must forge both the quartz‑anchored signature and the vine nonce for every replica, inflating the cost roughly linearly with the number of fake identities.
